title: Microsoft Purview: legacy Teams retention policies will stop covering Copilot interactions
summary: The briefing accurately reports the planned loss of Copilot coverage, the January rollout and the replacement retention controls. Its licensing and billing statements are supported, and it explicitly identifies the conflicting PowerShell guidance. The portal route could include the wizard's default administrative-unit step.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to convert legacy Teams retention policies that also cover Copilot into Teams-only policies.
claims.quote: these legacy Teams retention policies will be converted to—and treated as—Teams-only policies. They will no longer implicitly govern Copilot workloads.

claims.claim: Some existing Teams-scoped retention policies currently also apply to Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions.
claims.quote: Some existing retention policies scoped to Microsoft Teams may currently also apply to Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions.

claims.claim: Get output for legacy policies continues to show MicrosoftTeams rather than TeamsChatUserInteractions despite Teams-only processing.
claims.quote: doing a Get command on 'Teams chats and Copilot interactions' policies from cmdlet will still show the policy covering teams+copilot i.e. MicrosoftTeams and NOT TeamsChatUserInteractions but while processing; they will ONLY cover Teams Interactions.

claims.claim: The policy inventory is in Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies.

claims.claim: Get-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Identity "<policy name>" -DistributionDetail | Format-List inventories the specified policy and its locations in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: Get-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Identity "Regulation 123 Compliance" -DistributionDetail | Format-List ... including accurate values for the DistributionStatus and *Location properties.

claims.claim: The printed portal route opens a new static retention policy and selects Microsoft Copilot experiences.
claims.quote: For the Assign admin units page, keep the default of Full directory. ... For the Choose the type of retention policy to create page, select Adaptive or Static ... On the Choose locations to apply the policy page ... Microsoft Copilot experiences
claims.fix: Set controls[1].ui.path and its rendered copy to 'Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies > New retention policy > Assign admin units > Full directory > Choose the type of retention policy to create > Static > Choose locations to apply the policy > Microsoft Copilot experiences'. The omitted wizard page keeps its default and does not invalidate the route.

claims.claim: The configuration guide shows Set-AppRetentionCompliancePolicy -Identity "<policy name>" -Applications "User:M365Copilot" to add Copilot to an existing policy for newer locations.
claims.quote: To add Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions to an existing retention policy for newer locations ... Set-AppRetentionCompliancePolicy -Identity “<policy name>” -Applications "User:M365Copilot"

claims.claim: The cmdlet reference instead marks Microsoft Copilot experiences as preview and requires User:M365Copilot,CopilotForSecurity,CopilotinFabricPowerBI,CopilotStudio,CopilotinBusinessApplicationplatformsSales,SQLCopilot together.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot experiences: Currently in Preview. You must use all of the following values at the same time: "User:M365Copilot,CopilotForSecurity,CopilotinFabricPowerBI,CopilotStudio,CopilotinBusinessApplicationplatformsSales,SQLCopilot"
